evidence_role.label: Evidence Role
evidence_role.description: Classifies how a record may be used as evidence or routing context.

terms.label: Source Evidence
terms.description: Admissible source-grounded evidence that may support answer claims when cited to the underlying source.
allowed_usage: Use only for source-supported facts, events, or text spans that can ground an answer claim.
disallowed_usage: Do not use for diagnostics, routing hints, summaries, or unsupported candidates.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with source_evidence.
terms.admissibility_notes: May support answer claims when coupled to source citation/provenance.

terms.label: Supporting Context
terms.description: Context that can help interpret source evidence but should not carry the answer claim by itself.
allowed_usage: Use for nearby context that frames an admissible source.
disallowed_usage: Do not cite as the sole basis for a factual answer claim.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with supporting_context.
terms.admissibility_notes: Can accompany source evidence but is not sufficient alone.

terms.label: Routing Hint
terms.description: Navigation metadata used to find likely relevant material; it is not source evidence.
allowed_usage: Use for route, lane, or index signals that help retrieval find candidates.
disallowed_usage: Do not admit as source evidence or treat as proof of a claim.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with routing_hint.
terms.admissibility_notes: Not source evidence; routing-only values must be backed by a real source before answering.

terms.label: Diagnostic Only
terms.description: Internal diagnostic output for evaluation, debugging, or reporting; it is not source evidence.
allowed_usage: Use for validator, report, or debug artifacts that explain system behavior.
disallowed_usage: Do not expose as source truth or admit as evidence for answer claims.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with diagnostic_only.
terms.admissibility_notes: Not source evidence and not promotion-safe as answer support.

terms.label: Derived Summary
terms.description: A summary derived from source material; useful for orientation but not independently admissible as source evidence.
allowed_usage: Use when the value summarizes or compresses other source-backed material.
disallowed_usage: Do not cite as source evidence unless the original source support is also present.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with derived_summary.
terms.admissibility_notes: Not source evidence by itself; source citations must point through to original material.

terms.label: Candidate Evidence
terms.description: Proposed evidence that still needs validation against source material.
allowed_usage: Use for candidate evidence awaiting source verification.
disallowed_usage: Do not treat as answer-supporting source evidence until validated.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with candidate_evidence.
terms.admissibility_notes: Candidate only until validated against source support.

terms.label: Not Admissible
terms.description: Content that must not be used as evidence for answer claims.
allowed_usage: Use when policy, provenance, or source quality blocks evidentiary use.
disallowed_usage: Do not admit as source evidence or promote as answer support.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with not_admissible.
terms.admissibility_notes: Explicitly not source evidence.

terms.label: Navigation Only
terms.description: A navigational marker that helps locate material but is not itself evidentiary.
allowed_usage: Use for anchors, routes, or wayfinding structures.
disallowed_usage: Do not treat as proof of campaign facts.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with navigation_only.
terms.admissibility_notes: Navigation-only; requires separate source evidence for claims.

authority_state.label: Authority State
authority_state.description: Distinguishes kinds of truth, authority, and source support.

terms.label: Played Truth
terms.description: Information established in actual play or canonical session recap.
allowed_usage: Use for source-supported events or facts established in play.
disallowed_usage: Do not use for GM prep that has not occurred in play or unsupported inference.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with played_truth.
terms.admissibility_notes: Source-grounded played truth may support promoted records when citations are present.

terms.label: Canonical Recap
terms.description: Information asserted by an accepted canonical recap.
allowed_usage: Use for facts represented in the canonical recap surface.
disallowed_usage: Do not use for loose notes, drafts, or private prep unless accepted as recap.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with canonical_recap.

terms.description: A candidate is blocked by a policy or scope constraint.
allowed_usage: Use when rules prevent use regardless of structure.
disallowed_usage: Do not bypass policy via promotion.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with blocked_by_policy.
terms.admissibility_notes: Policy block must be explicit.

terms.label: Missing Source
terms.description: A candidate lacks required source support.
allowed_usage: Use when provenance or citation is absent.
disallowed_usage: Do not validate as source-grounded.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with missing_source.
terms.admissibility_notes: Missing source blocks evidence use.

terms.label: Conflicted
terms.description: A candidate has unresolved conflicts.
allowed_usage: Use when sources or validations disagree.
disallowed_usage: Do not present as settled.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with conflicted.
terms.admissibility_notes: Conflict-aware review required.

promotion_state.label: Promotion State
promotion_state.description: Classifies readiness for promotion from experiment output toward durable use.

terms.label: Not Promoted
terms.description: No promotion has occurred.
allowed_usage: Use for baseline or local-only records.
disallowed_usage: Do not treat as approved for durable use.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with not_promoted.
terms.admissibility_notes: Default non-promoted state.

terms.label: Shadow Only
terms.description: Approved only for shadow-mode experiment use.
allowed_usage: Use for non-production graph experiments.
disallowed_usage: Do not affect production retrieval.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with shadow_only.
terms.admissibility_notes: Shadow only.

terms.label: Report Only
terms.description: Approved only for reports and diagnostics.
allowed_usage: Use for operator visibility without retrieval influence.
disallowed_usage: Do not use for retrieval expansion.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with report_only.
terms.admissibility_notes: Report-only admission.

terms.label: Validated For Experiment
terms.description: Validated enough for experiment use but not durable promotion.
allowed_usage: Use after experiment validators pass.
disallowed_usage: Do not imply production approval.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with validated_for_experiment.
terms.admissibility_notes: Experiment-scoped validation.

terms.label: Approved For Promotion
terms.description: Reviewed and ready for promotion, pending promotion action.
allowed_usage: Use after explicit approval.
disallowed_usage: Do not use before validation and policy checks.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with approved_for_promotion.
terms.admissibility_notes: Promotion gate passed.

terms.label: Promoted
terms.description: Promoted to the next approved durable stage.
allowed_usage: Use only after explicit promotion.
disallowed_usage: Do not use to override authority, visibility, or evidence restrictions.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with promoted.
terms.admissibility_notes: Promotion preserves admissibility constraints.

terms.label: Rolled Back
terms.description: A prior promotion was reverted.
allowed_usage: Use for rollback/audit trail.
disallowed_usage: Do not treat as currently promoted.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with rolled_back.
terms.admissibility_notes: Rollback state.

terms.label: Blocked
terms.description: Promotion is blocked.
allowed_usage: Use when promotion criteria fail.
disallowed_usage: Do not promote until blocker is resolved.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with blocked.
terms.admissibility_notes: Blocked state.

validation_severity.label: Validation Severity
validation_severity.description: Classifies validation outcomes emitted by no-LLM validators or future graph checks.

terms.label: Info
terms.description: Informational validation output.
allowed_usage: Use for non-blocking observations.
disallowed_usage: Do not use for blocking failures.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with info.
terms.admissibility_notes: Informational only.

terms.label: Warning
terms.description: Non-fatal validation concern.
allowed_usage: Use for issues that deserve attention but may not block.
disallowed_usage: Do not ignore if promotion policy treats warnings as blockers.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with warning.
terms.admissibility_notes: Warning semantics depend on policy.

terms.label: Error
terms.description: Validation failure that should block readiness.
allowed_usage: Use for failed required checks.
disallowed_usage: Do not mark registry ready while errors remain.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with error.
terms.admissibility_notes: Blocks success.

terms.label: Fatal
terms.description: Validation failure severe enough to stop processing.
allowed_usage: Use for corrupt input or impossible continuation.
disallowed_usage: Do not continue normal validation after fatal errors.
examples: A future graph-memory report labels a candidate with fatal.
terms.admissibility_notes: Hard stop.

promotion_semantics: allowed_graph_record_states means the controlled term may appear on records in those lifecycle states; it does not mean a claim is admissible as source evidence, player-visible, or safe to promote without source, authority, visibility, and validation checks.
